summary: New public read routes GET /v1/fleet/status, /v1/fleet/membership, /v1/fleet/admission-residue and /v1/fleet/invites; internal routes (/v1/internal/...) now refuse seat callers

replay.detail: No claim is written or read differently.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: A request from a process running under an agent seat's harness to any /v1/internal/ route is refused with foreign-agent-actor, by any method. The node's own processes, which run in no harness (the replication worker, local adapters, the operator's CLI), are unaffected. New public routes answer what a seat may read, with the same handlers: GET /v1/fleet/status, /v1/fleet/membership, /v1/fleet/admission-residue and /v1/fleet/invites. st fleet status, st fleet wait, st fleet invites, remote terminal attach and the client library's fleet_membership read the public routes and fall back to the internal ones on a daemon that predates them. Fleet changes (invite, remove, leave, transports) stay internal, so a seat cannot make them. During a host's upgrade, an older st already running inside a seat may see one fleet read refused (st fleet status, wait or invites, or a remote terminal attach); retry it after the upgrade, when the st on disk is the new one and reads the public routes.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

manual.detail: No manual step. A replication worker started by hand from a seat's shell is refused; run it as the service, or outside the seat.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting lets seat callers reach internal routes again.
